sutta: in the woods and the experiences so now we come to 9.13 it's on page 302 on one occasion the number of monks were dwelling among the coastal lands in a certain woodland ticket they were restless after personally they dropped down rambling in their talk model minded without clear comprehension unconcentrated scattered brain lose in the sense faculties then the developer that inhabited that woodland ticket having compassion for those monks desiring their good desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in them approach them and address them in verses in the past the monks lived happily the disciples of gotama without wishes they sought their arms without wishes they used their lodgings having known the world's impermanence they made an end to suffering but now like hate men in a village they make themselves hard to maintain they eat and eat and then lie down infatuated in others homes having reverently saluted the sangha i hear speak only about some they are rejected without protector become just like the dead my statement is made with reference to those who dwell in negligence as for those who dwell in diligence to them i humbly pay homage and those monks stirred up by the devata acquired a sense of urgency this is another one of the sutras where the deva out of compassion for the lazy monks come to stir them up so that they become more diligent because if they know that somebody is  watching them then they are not become so lazy
